title: S5: active skill routing for trusted builtin skills: selected compact skills are presented in the worker packet (Level 2), static exposure is switched off for Claude workers, recovery reads are measured; gated by [skills] mode and a safety refusal
spec:
Program brief .orchestrator/roadmap-skills.md P8 step 7, P10, P12 (skills part), P30 recovery (P37 stage 5). Depends on T-0913 (skill_router.select, [skills] mode, skill_selection rows, skills_selected in packet meta) and T-0894 (skills_used detection). Facts (Planner grep): Claude workers are launched by spawn.run_claude as `claude -p <prompt> --model ... --allowedTools ... [--disallowedTools ...]` with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account (spawn.py ~781-795); the CLI offers `--disable-slash-commands` ("Disable all skills") and `--plugin-dir`; worktrees carry the repo's committed .claude/skills symlinks, which is today's static exposure; skills with scripts are invoked through `bash skills/<role>/<name>/scripts/...`, which the allowlists already permit (Bash(bash skills/*)); Codex executors get implement-spec through AGENTS.md; skills_registry.render(id, 2) gives the compact body.
Do:
1. Presentation: when [skills] mode == "active", the worker packet gains a section "## skills" carrying, for each selected skill, a header line "### <id> (v<version>)" and its Level 2 rendering; the section sits after the role instructions and before the task contract sections; for Codex executors the same section goes into the execute packet (implement-spec always selected for executors, so Codex sees the compact body in the packet as well as via AGENTS.md). Ambiguous candidates are listed as one Level 0 line each under "### available on request" so a worker can Read skills/<id>/SKILL.md when it needs one.
2. Exposure: in active mode Claude workers are launched with `--disable-slash-commands` so the static .claude/skills descriptions no longer load; nothing in .claude/skills, the repo or the worktree changes. In shadow and off the launch is byte-identical to today (test asserts the argv).
3. Telemetry: skill_tokens_presented_l2 in packet meta and run context; the skill_selection decision row's selected = presented ids, mode = active; skills_used detection (S1b) extended: a Read of skills/<role>/<name>/SKILL.md by the worker, or a bash invocation of that skill's script, counts as a use; a use of a skill that was not presented counts as a skill_recovery (S3 metric).
4. Safety refusal: active is refused (falls back to shadow with one notify line) when skill_scorecard shows fewer than 30 shadow selection rows for the role over the last 7 days, or a skill_recovery_rate above [skills] max_recovery (new key, default 0.10) for that role. Planner role is never switched (the interactive Planner keeps its own skills).
5. docs/skill-intelligence/06-active-routing.md (≤60 lines): mechanism, the refusal rules, how to read the recovery rate, revert path ([skills] mode shadow restores static exposure on the next spawn).
Tests (unittest): tests/test_spawn.py::test_active_skills_section_carries_level2_of_selected_only, ::test_active_launch_adds_disable_slash_commands_and_shadow_does_not, ::test_active_refused_without_shadow_evidence_or_with_high_recovery, ::test_skill_use_detected_from_read_of_skill_file_and_script_invocation; tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_presented_tokens_and_recovery_from_active_rows. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally. Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.

spec_review_risks.issue: Every prompts/*.md template (execute.md, review.md, spec-review.md, scout.md) substitutes {{packet}} as a single opaque block at the very top of the prompt, before all role-instruction prose. Spec step 1 asks for the new '## skills' section to sit 'after the role instructions and before the task contract sections', but the packet (built entirely inside spawn.py, which is in scope) has no slot that lands after role instructions — achieving that placement literally requires restructuring these template files, which are not in scope. As written this criterion cannot be satisfied without touching files outside scope.

_skill_routing (and executor.py's _route_skills) unconditionally notify 'skill routing active is shadow-only until Stage 5; exposure is unchanged' the first time mode=="active" is observed, latched by a boolean that never resets. This spec is Stage 5 (docs/skill-intelligence/04-routing.md: 'Stage 5 will make it control exposure'), so once a role's active mode is accepted (not refused), that message becomes false but the spec never asks to remove or replace it.

The skill_selection decision_log.record call inside _skill_routing (and the matching one in executor.py's _route_skills) never includes a role field, only task_class/triggers/mandatory. Step 4's refusal rule needs 'fewer than 30 shadow selection rows for the role over the last 7 days', but neither decision_log (no role, and skill_scorecard.build() ignores decision_log entirely) nor skill_scorecard.build() (no time filtering, reads runs/*.jsonl completion context, not decision events) currently exposes a role- and time-windowed shadow-row count. The spec doesn't say which of these two data sources to extend, or that role needs to be added to the decision row at all.

Step 4 says the Planner role is exempt from the active/shadow switch, but no in-scope call site ever invokes _skill_routing/_route_skills/skill_router.select with role="planner": headless Planner launches are built independently in planner_shadow.py, which never calls promotion.mode("skill_routing", ...) or skill_router at all. The MANDATORY["planner"] entry here is already dead code for this pipeline, so the exemption is unreachable and untestable as scoped.

_packet_body's 4800-char trim loop only knows a fixed tuple of trimmable sections (dependencies, evidence, decisions, gotchas, symbols, relevant_tests); acceptance is deliberately exempt and grows the header instead. The new '## skills' section (mandatory + up to max_selected L2 renderings) isn't mentioned as trimmable or exempt, so a large presented-skill payload either silently blows the budget with no trim path, or needs to be added to the rotation without the same overflow-header protection given to acceptance. The spec doesn't say which.

events.reason: superseded 06:25 by T-0935 (spec v2 after T-0930: skills section first in packet, own cap, stale notify removed, role on rows + selection_rows, no Planner exemption)
